title: Calibration fit objective and conditioned systematic propagation

scopes.title: Fitted calibration uncertainty versus measured optical probability
scopes.checked_claim: Brout Sec3.1 defines survey-filter offsets through observed tertiary-star magnitude differences and synthetic CALSPEC/NGSL transformations. Eq5 is a weighted objective with scatter/N, error floors and zero-centred prior penalties; emcee produces a fitted uncertainty covariance. Sec4.3 and AppendixA propagate correlated zeropoint realizations through SALT2 retraining and subsequent light-curve fitting. Uncorrelated mean-wavelength shifts enter retraining and affect subsequent fits through the resulting SALT2 surfaces. Sec6 explicitly omits zeropoint–wavelength correlations from those systematics. These are conditioned estimation and propagation choices.
scopes.unresolved: No normalized native likelihood or optical-state/arrival/QE/gain/extraction/censoring law follows from this objective or fitted covariance. Actual star/error inputs, fitting implementation, coordinate measure/normalization, joint zeropoint–wavelength covariance and draw generator remain unverified. Preserve 105-filter prose versus 102 fitted-release coordinates, unresolved machine aliases/passbands/events and shared calibration covariance.

limitations: The paper’s covariance concerns fitted magnitude offsets; choosing a Gaussian or other normalized native density from it requires an additional declared statistical model and source/input evidence.
Eq5 prints a half-weight prior term and compact summation/index notation. Its prose assigns priors per survey-filter; no summation repair, log-density normalization or sampler target is inferred.

Correlations among zeropoint offsets differ from the chosen uncorrelated mean-wavelength perturbations. The source omits their cross-correlations; physical zero covariance or independent calibration measurements is not established.
Nine mock realizations are systematic propagation samples, not nine measured optical states, a finite population law or observed probability masses.
The prior Table3/NPZ count discrepancy, PS1 Public/PS1SNe/Foundation mapping, CFA3S r/i versus R/I, passband/zeropoint sign and event-level joins remain unresolved.

Source selection cuts, synthetic standards, repeated telescope calibrations, prior widths, survey weights and uncertainty floors condition the fit. Raw catalogues, standards, response curves and full dependency covariance remain unverified.

SALT2 retraining and distance covariance propagation remain empirical and conditioned; no template-format, first-principles luminosity, numerical accuracy or measured detector likelihood is qualified.

The checked wavelength-shift pathway is retraining followed by downstream fitting with the changed SALT2 surfaces. No separate direct wavelength-shift implementation in the fitting passbands is certified.
